item.title: Politician who was intentionally hit by car loses both her legs
item.description: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines, who was intentionally hit by a car in an apparent political attack, has lost both of her legs, her husband said.

item.title: American Stephen Hubbard released by Russia, Trump confirms
item.description: Russia has released Stephen Hubbard, an American deemed wrongfully detained by the U.S. for more than four years.

item.title: Up to 20% of MS diagnoses may be wrong, like Christina Applegate's
item.description: A multiple sclerosis expert answers questions about MS misdiagnosis after Christina Applegate said she doesn't have the chronic condition after all.

item.title: Russia frees American Stephen Hubbard
item.description: Russia has freed Stephen Hubbard, an American who the U.S. Department of State says was wrongfully detained after he was accused of being a mercenary for Ukraine. CBS News intelligence and national security reporter Olivia Gazis and White House producer Kristin Brown have more details.

item.title: Chemical leak in Toledo forces evacuations, shelter-in-place
item.description: A massive chemical leak in Toledo, Ohio, is forcing some people out of their homes while others have been told to shelter in place.

item.title: Norah O'Donnell: What I learned from my melanoma diagnosis
item.description: More people are diagnosed with skin cancer each year in the U.S. than all other cancers combined.

item.title: Electricity bills force 1 in 5 to cut back on food, survey finds
item.description: Americans living on a fixed income are particularly vulnerable when electricity costs surge, a Consumer Reports expert says.

item.title: What You Can Learn From My Skin Cancer Diagnosis
item.description: Ten years ago, Norah was diagnosed with melanoma. It was a wakeup call that changed her relationship with the sun and made her want to shine a light on the importance of early skin cancer detection. On this week's episode of Healthful, Norah's dermatologist, Dr. Elizabeth Hale, discusses ways to prevent skin cancer, where melanoma commonly appears on women vs. men, and alarming trends around tanning.

item.title: Student says she was sexually assaulted at Arizona frat house
item.description: The sexual assault allegations surfaced two weeks after the university had suspended activities for its 21 fraternities amid reports of misconduct.

item.title: Armed federal agents knock on doors looking for noncitizen voters
item.description: Armed and in uniform, agents from the Department of Homeland Security have been knocking on doors to ask residents about their immigration status whether they're registered to vote.

item.title: Memphis fails to pass 1-year data center moratorium, opts for shorter-term ban
item.description: Memphis has become a hotspot for data centers driven by Elon Musk's SpaceXAI.

item.title: Ohio race takes ugly turn with ad featuring Amy Acton's mother
item.description: Democrat Amy Acton's estranged mother calls her a liar in a new GOP ad. Acton's brother says the ad marks a "despicable low" and says their stepfather sexually abused Acton when she was a child.

item.title: Florida executes man who killed deputy after fighting for gun
item.description: Florida carried out its 18th execution this year under Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis' aggressive use of the death penalty.

item.title: Musk chose to restrict Ukraine's access to SpaceX network, sources say
item.description: A decision by Elon Musk led to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's satellite communications network, people familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Iran touts closest ever ties with Russia, contradicting Trump
item.description: Iran says its ties with Russia are stronger than ever after a visit by Putin's top envoy, challenging Trump's assertion that Moscow isn't helping Iran in the war.

item.title: The AI doom scenario you've never heard of may be hardest to stop
item.description: The time to prepare for "gradual disempowerment" is now, according to researchers. One calls it "a civilization-scale problem."

item.title: The often neglected AI doom scenario that poses a different kind of threat to humanity
item.description: Some researchers warn that as artificial intelligence agents take on more and more tasks, humans could end up giving up their critical thinking skills in a scenario they call "gradual disempowerment." Jay Chooi, co-founder and CEO of Robocurve, a company that tracks AI-driven robots, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: The risks of trusting personal AI agents with your money, data
item.description: With personal AI agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots hitting the market, experts are warning of the risks associated with giving these chatbots access to your data and money. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Democratic presidential contenders to gather for post-midterm summit in Denver
item.description: Potential 2028 Democratic presidential contenders are set to gather in Denver for a post-midterm summit. CBS News political director Fin Gómez reports.

item.title: Elon Musk chose to restrict Ukraine's use of SpaceX satellite network, sources say
item.description: Elon Musk chose to limit Ukraine's access to SpaceX's satellite service, affecting drone operations, sources say.

item.title: What to know about Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis
item.description: Jalen Hurts' agent and the Eagles said in a statement Monday his "prognosis is very good, and we anticipate a full recovery."

item.title: Trump says U.S. has gotten "nothing" from Ukraine
item.description: President Trump on Tuesday said the U.S. has "given a lot" to Ukraine and gotten "nothing" in return amid Russia's ongoing war with the country. CBS News' Aaron MacLean has more.

item.title: Cornell responds to Jane Doe letter saying she felt disbelieved
item.description: Cornell has denied claims made in a letter from a former student, known as Jane Doe, about a remark by the school's president.

item.title: Doctor explains how a misdiagnosis of multiple sclerosis happens amid Christina Applegate news
item.description: Actress Christina Applegate revealed on her podcast Tuesday that she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis. CBS News' medical correspondent Dr. Cèline Gounder explains what could have happened.

item.title: French government extends curfews after riots sweep across the country
item.description: French authorities are extending curfews and increasing the police presence in public spaces as President Emmanuel Macron's government tries to regain control after rioters torched buildings and looted thousands of businesses this weekend.

item.title: 10/20: CBS Evening News
item.description: A brake issue prompts an American Airlines emergency landing; Christina Applegate reveals a devastating misdiagnosis.

item.title: Trump says U.S. will pay fraud whistleblowers, and he'll decide who is paid
item.description: President Trump said successful whistleblowers will get 1% of any fraud they report, although there may be limits.

item.title: 10/20: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: 14 days until midterm contests; President Trump looks to boost Republicans in North Carolina elections.

item.title: Gun used in Bend school shooting was birthday gift from shooter's mom
item.description: The Maverick 88 pump-action 12-gauge shotgun was purchased legally in August 2026 by Shauntai Nickerson, the mother of the shooter, and given to him for recreational use, sources told CBS News.

item.title: Trump announces $8 billion in diesel relief for U.S. farmers
item.description: The USDA said farmers don't need crop insurance to qualify and can prepare to apply by creating a Login.gov account.
